The reader identifies Arabic muštāq/šwq. This is a comparative contact attribution, not proof that an Arabic-derived form has a productive native Turoyo paradigm. The assigned surface headword štq is retained with an editorial headword question.
An experiencer and a l-marked desired homeland are explicit; the supplied verse does not itself name the experiencers as Israelites. That reader identification is not added to the lexical example.
The copula is state predication, not a light-verb idiom. No separate homeland-longing technical or figurative sense is needed.
Should this be indexed as the contact participle under surface štq, under šwq, or as a lexical adjective cross-reference? Native finite bases remain unattested.
Is məštaq invariant with plural wayye here, and are gender/number alternatives used in Turoyo? One predicate cannot establish an agreement paradigm.
